description: issue #932, the EXECUTE half of the pair whose check half is `command-body-no-value-check` — the same source, so the two stages are pinned to the same answer for one program: the same `ol-no-value` code, the same `form` param, and the same line/column range, each fixture's span naming its own document. The runtime used to carry a verbatim copy of the checker's three-name command list, so BOTH stages were silent here: agreement on the wrong answer. No event is emitted at all, because the fault is decided before Phase 2. Under the `runUnchecked` opt-out the trace stops at the `instruction` event for the assignment: the body's final statement is a Command, so `runComprehensionBody` reports no-value for the first element before evaluating it, and no `move`/`draw-segment` event is ever emitted — the same order the `print` spelling follows. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`.
